Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILGt4APOLCOM Center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. s. 201 ATTY. ANNA FATIMA R. CHAVEZ Attorney IV Office of the City Legal Officer City of Puerto Princesa, Palawan Dear Atty. Chavez: MERICRÆOLOCAL EZEUVE 1b MAY TION RECORDSSECIION CN This pertains to your letter dated March 6, 2017 requesting legal opinion relative to the investigation of administrative complaints filed against city public health workers of the City Health Office of Puerto Princesa City. Your letter substantially reads: "(A) barangay health worker filed a complaint for discourtesy and grave misconduct against a nurse of the said City Health Office. x x x we are obliged to dismiss the complaint [without prejudice to its refilling(sic)] due to lack of jurisdiction. This is because pursuant to Section II of R.A. (No) 7302, otherwise known as "The Magna Carta for Public Health Workers", the jurisdiction to hear and try administrative complaints against public health workers is vested upon the committee created for the purpose composed of the provincial health Officer as chairperson, a representative of any existing national or provincial public health worker's organization or in its absence its local counterpart and a supervisor of the district. x x x. Currently, there is already such a committee existing in the provincial level, the PHO Investigation Committee. " From the foregoing, you wish to be enlightened on the following matters: I. Whether or not an administrative complaint against City Public Health Workers of the City of Puerto Princesa is within the jurisdiction of the Provincial Health Office Investigation 1

2. 3. Committee of the Province of Palawan considering that the City of Puerto Princesa is a highly urbanized city; If in the affirmative, should the complaint be directly lodged with the Committee or should the complaint be first endorsed by the City Mayor considering that he is the Disciplining Authority; Whether or not the City Government of Puerto Princesa can create the same Committee with the City Health Officer as the chairperson. At the outset, let it be emphasized that as a matter of policy, our Department cannot accommodate your request in keeping with DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-011 as supplemented by Memorandum Order No. 2010-022 which enumerates matters ought not to be addressed by this Department, viz: (1) those containing facts that are justiciable in nature; (2) those presumptively valid acts; e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances;" (3) those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation; and (4) those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government. However, for purposes of academic discussion, this Department has the following disquisition. As you have correctly pointed out, apropos is Section II of Republic Act No. 7305 which explicitly provides: "Section II. Administrative Charges. - Administrative charges against public health workers shall be heard by a committee composed of the provincial health officer of the province where the public health worker belongs, as chairperson, a representative of any existing national or provincial public health workers' organization or in its absence its local counterpart and a supervisor of the district, the last two (2) to be designated by the provincial health officer mentioned above. The committee shall submit its findings and recommendations to the Secretary of Health within thirty (30) days from the termination of the hearings. Where the provincial health officer is an interested party, all the members of the committee shall be appointed by the Secretary of Health. " (emphasis supplied) March 4, 2010 2 September 17, 2010 2

Similarly, the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of R.A. No. 7305 provides: "RULE XI. Administrative Discipline SECTION 1. No administrative charges shall be filed against a public health worker unless an existing prima facie evidence established in the preliminary investigation/hearing. Administrative charges shall be made known to him/her and heard by the committee created for the purpose. xxx xxx SECTION 3. Local health workers' organizations duly recognized by the Local Government Unit shall be represented in the investigating committee. Xxx xxx xxx SECTION 5. Administrative charges against a public health worker shall be heard by a committee composed of the provincial health officer of the province where the public health worker belongs, as chairperson, a representative of any existing national or provincial health worker's organization or in its absence its local counterpart and a supervisor of the office mentioned above. The committee shall submit its recommendation to the Secretary of Health or the appropriate disciplining authority within thirty (30) days from the termination of the investigation/hearings. Where the provincial health officer is an interested party in the case, all the members of the committee shall be appointed by the Secretary of Health or the appropriate disciplining authority. (emphasis supplied) Administrative charges against public health workers are under the jurisdiction of an Investigation Committee composed of the Provincial Health Officer of the province where the public health worker belongs, as Chairperson, a representative of any existing national or provincial public health workers' organization or in its absence its local counterpart, and a supervisor of the district, the last two (2) to be designated by the provincial health officer. Said Investigating Committee is vested with the authority to hear and investigate administrative complaints against public health workers and shall submit its recommendation to the Secretary of Health or the appropriate disciplining authority within thirty (30) days from the termination of the investigation/hearings. Notably, the law is too specific that it only mandates the creation of such Committee to be chaired by the Provincial Health Officer. It does not 3

provide for the creation of similar committee in various levels of local government units i.e., city or municipality. If it had the intention to create it also in other local government units, it should have clearly provided for the same. Likewise, a cursory reading of Republic Act No. 59063 reveals no provision regarding discipline of public health workers. There being no ambiguity in the law, administrative complaints filed against public health workers of the City of Puerto Princesa, though a highly urbanized city, are cognizable by the Investigation Committee specifically created for that purpose by R.A. No. 7305. Moreover, the law does not require prior indorsement of any administrative complaint against public health workers by the City Mayor before the Investigating Committee chaired by the Provincial Health Officer may take cognizance thereof. A cardinal rule in statutory construction is that when the law is clear and free from any doubt or ambiguity, there is no room for construction or interpretation. There is only room for application.4 We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. uly yours, AUSTERE A.
